note: Captured once from the published effect-dynamodb@1.40.0 and @effect-dynamodb/schema@1.40.0, installed outside the repo and run by a scratch script against DynamoDB Local. Entity Doc over { id, group, lists, rl: Record<string, number[]>, whole: Record<string, number> }, lists configured { storedAs: SparseMap({ prefix: 'l' }) }, rl { storedAs: SparseMap({ prefix: 'r' }), field: 'rw' }, whole { storedAs: SparseMap({ prefix: 'w' }), field: 'wh' }; entity Peer over { id, group, lists }, lists { storedAs: SparseMap({ prefix: 'p' }) }; both with a byGroup index in collection 'group', on DynamoSchema.make({ name: 'es', version: 1 }). Rows: w, put with every list { a: [10, 20, 30] } and whole { k: 1 }; e, the renamed maps as entries (put, then a raw SET r#a, w#k REMOVE rw, wh); x, the renamed maps whole and empty beside entries r#a = [1, 2, 3], w#k = 5; y, rl { a: [7, 8, 9] } and whole { k: 1 } beside r#a = [1, 2, 3], w#k = 5, w#j = 2; Peer p with lists { a: [10, 20, 30] }. Each case sends one select through Docs.byGroup or the collection. Recorded: its outcome (a result, or a failure's tag and the first line of its message), every request it sent, whole and in order, every row of the table after it, and what an unselected byGroup read gave. The table's name is replaced by <table>, UUIDs by <token> and timestamps by <time>. Never regenerate it: it is the record of what 1.40.0 did.
